note: The new ot-face model stores the face pointer as the first field of the heap-allocated hb_ot_face_data_t, followed by lazy loaders for accelerators and tables.
The hb_ot_face_data_t is heap-allocated via calloc, so the face field and all lazy loaders live in heap memory.
The face pointer is stored in the first field of the heap-allocated hb_ot_face_data_t.
A stack-allocated hb_closure_context_t is created and passed by pointer through the GSUB closure recursion.
The GSUB table is obtained via _get_gsub(face), which dereferences hb_ot_face_data(face)->GSUB->table.
During GSUB closure recursion, dispatch_recurse_func re-fetches the GSUB table using _get_gsub_relaxed(c->face), which calls hb_ot_face_data(c->face)->GSUB->get_relaxed().
The lazy loader computes the face pointer by subtracting WheresData from the loader address, reading the face field from the heap-allocated hb_ot_face_data_t.
The accelerator is created by calling init on the face pointer obtained from the heap-allocated hb_ot_face_data_t.
The subsetting code path stack-allocates an old-style cmap accelerator_t, which is unrelated to the new lazy-loader model and does not use the heap-allocated hb_ot_face_data_t.
Similarly, a stack-allocated glyf accelerator_t is created in the subsetting path, again not using the new lazy-loader model.
The closure recursion passes the stack-allocated hb_closure_context_t c by pointer, and dispatch_recurse_func dereferences c->face to re-fetch the GSUB table.

The GSUB closure is invoked with the stack-allocated context, and the recursion re-fetches the GSUB table via the heap-allocated hb_ot_face_data_t, causing a stack-use-after-return when the context or the face data is accessed after the stack frame is gone.
